question: Name the place where “independent” parallel government by Indians was established during the Quit India movement as a mark of revolt against British government.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Satara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During the Quit India Movement of 1942, parallel governments were formed in several parts of India as an act of defiance against British rule.
 
• **Satara** in Maharashtra was notable for establishing a parallel government, often referred to as the "Patri Sarkar."
 
• This government was led by local leaders such as Krantisinh Nana Patil, who played a significant role in its formation and operation.
 
• The Satara parallel government took over the administration, implemented its own laws, and provided services to the local populace, effectively functioning as an independent entity for a period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quit India Movement:**

 
 
• The Quit India Movement, also known as the August Movement, was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on 8th August 1942 at the Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee (AICC).
 
• It demanded an end to British rule in India and was marked by widespread acts of defiance, including strikes, protests, and the establishment of parallel governments.
 
 
 
• **Patri Sarkar (Satara Parallel Government):**
 
 
• The term "Patri Sarkar" translates to "Rebel Government" and it was established in Satara district to provide an alternative to British rule.
 
• The parallel government collected taxes, settled disputes, maintained law and order, and conducted welfare activities.
 
 
 
• **Krantisinh Nana Patil:**
 
 
• Nana Patil was a prominent freedom fighter who led the parallel government in Satara and was known for his revolutionary activities against the British.
 
• He played a crucial role in organizing the local population and ensuring the smooth functioning of the parallel government.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Parallel Governments:**
 
 
• The formation of parallel governments demonstrated the capability of Indians to self-govern and highlighted the widespread discontent with British rule.
 
• These governments inspired further resistance and contributed to the momentum of the Indian independence movement.
